rule: packages depend downward only; allow lists are exhaustive — any internal dependency or source import not listed here is a violation

@sceneaxi/site-umbrella.note: ADR 0022 (amended 2026-07-26): the umbrella owns every viewport — both the public /open surface and the entitled Minimum E2 /editor surface — so it alone may consume the ADR 0002 presentation seam to draw a real artifact into a browser canvas. It is also the one site wired to the identity plane (sceneaxi#131), so it alone may consume @sceneaxi/auth and @sceneaxi/billing, and only through the plug point src/lib/identity-plane.ts together with the deployment adapters it assembles in src/lib/provider-adapters.ts (sceneaxi#180) — two files and no more, so no route, page, component, or other src/lib module may name either package. Request code reaches that deployment authority only through the no-argument facade src/lib/request-authority.ts (ADR 0021's 2026-08-01 clarification): identity-plane.ts, provider-adapters.ts, and credit-webhook.ts are importable only by the sibling owners pinned for each — that facade among them for the two it drives — and the site's own root barrel, which re-exports all three, is importable by nothing, so a route, page, or component that names one — relatively, through a tsconfig alias or baseUrl, or through a const-bound dynamic import — is refused. The edge stops there — no kernel, orchestrator, authoring-core, profile, or Kids package — and the two catalog sites keep site-kit only, reaching identity through the same site-kit ports rather than a second auth stack.

@sceneaxi/site-kids.note: sceneaxi#200: the fully separate Kids origin is a self-contained Next install root with a closed in-memory activity table. It imports no SceneAxi package — including profile-kids and site-kit — and declares no provider, identity, billing, catalog, persistence, telemetry, or external-data dependency. Profile/site parity is gate-tested without creating a runtime edge, so kidsBoundary.allowedDependents remains empty.

@sceneaxi/desktop-linux.note: ADR 0024 and sceneaxi#192: the packaged Linux desktop application. It reuses the desktop-shell Engine Desktop visual model and session (never a second editor state machine), draws through the one ADR 0002 presentation seam in its renderer process, opens kernel sessions only through the orchestrator, and consumes the shared MountableScene payload from site-kit for both its starter composition and single-instance assistant output so what may be drawn stays decided in the hermetic gate. Deterministic local assistant work and an explicitly injected BYOK runner reach authoring-core; hosted refuses because the desktop has no identity plane. No profile package, Kids dependency, or auth/billing implementation crosses this tier.

@sceneaxi/desktop-windows.note: sceneaxi#204: isolated Windows signing/update packaging around the already-built desktop/linux application. Its source imports no SceneAxi package and adds only a Windows updater bootstrap; the staged runtime remains owned by desktop/linux, so there is no second editor, bridge, renderer, profile, Kids, or identity implementation.

@sceneaxi/desktop-macos.note: sceneaxi#194: the separate macOS packaging install root. Its only source-level workspace edge is schemas for the frozen seam; packaging stages the exact already-bundled desktop/linux runtime instead of importing or forking the desktop-shell, bridge, renderer, or engine implementation. The macOS-only bootstrap adds a fail-closed update check. No profile, Kids, auth/billing, plugin host, or second renderer owner.

kidsBoundary.rule: no package or app may depend on or import a Kids package; allowedDependents remains empty under the locked Kids isolation boundary

@sceneaxi/provider-<name>.arrives: additional provider adapters behind the Model Provider Port under the locked llm-provider-policy; ordinary ticketed work only

contracts.policy: schemas carry their own versions; the package root stays browser-safe while Node-only executable suites use explicit node subpaths; every consumer refuses major mismatches

core-train.policy: one shared semver train — a 'core release' covers all engine packages and authoring-core

profile.policy: independently versioned; each profile MUST declare sceneaxi.corePin (a semver range on the core train)

cli-protocol.policy: versions with its protocol envelope; output-schema changes are semver events

plugin-host.policy: independently versioned; consumes only public contracts from schemas; never engine packages or service locators

identity.policy: independently versioned; the identity/credits/billing plane consumes only public contracts from schemas (and, for billing, the auth seam); never engine packages, profiles, the CLI, or a service locator. Better Auth, Neon, and the Stripe API stay injected adapters (ADR 0021).

apps.policy: private, unpublished, unversioned beyond workspace bookkeeping

sites.policy: first-party deployable web surfaces. The umbrella and catalog sites consume only their charted public seams; never profiles, a service locator, or a Kids package. The single charted engine edge is ADR 0022 — the umbrella site may consume @sceneaxi/engine-presentation to draw every viewport it owns, both the public /open surface and the entitled /editor surface, and no other engine package is reachable from those sites. The dedicated Kids origin is the stricter exception: a self-contained Next install root with an empty SceneAxi allow list and no external data path. Framework dependencies stay in sites/ and out of the hermetic package tier.

desktop.policy: packaged desktop applications (ADR 0024); each is its own single-package install root outside the repository-root workspace so Electron never moves the hermetic root lockfile; consumes the desktop-shell visual model and public engine seams, never profiles, Kids, auth/billing, or a service locator; Electron and packaging toolchains stay in desktop/ and out of the hermetic package tier
